confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on three web searches of aggregated price sources run in November 2026. A Numbeo summary dated June 2026 gives about $25 for an inexpensive meal, $110 for a three-course meal for two and $8 for a 0.5L domestic draft beer. MyLifeElsewhere, updated July 2026, lists a $25 basic meal, an $8 pint and a $5.36 cappuccino. Expat Arrivals gives $5.75 for a cappuccino. Cocktail prices are about $15-18: Cities Insider lists standard cocktails at $15-18, and Expatistan gives about $18 but from only 7 price points. Glass of wine prices conflict, with $12-16 in one Cities Insider table and $14-22 in another Cities Insider article, so I set wine at $15. Beer may come in higher at bars in tourist areas, where it can be $9-10. The accommodation anchors are my own overall estimates for peak summer in July, using general knowledge only. I did not check any live listings or booking pages. Boston has few registered hostels, and its hotel rates in July are high, so the accommodation figures are much less certain than the food anchors. The 1-star and hostel-private figures are especially uncertain. The FX rate is the RBA observation for 18 November 2026, the latest available on the generation date, not a July 2026 rate.
comparable_city_reasoning: Boston prices are a little below New York City and similar to Washington DC or Chicago for dining and drinks. Accommodation is benchmarked against other high-cost US Northeast cities in peak summer.
